derived_theorem.reflection: If Gamma belongs to up_k(R,B), then by definition there exists Delta in R with Delta preccurlyeq Gamma. Since width(Delta)<=width(Gamma)<=k, at least one source Delta passes the width<=k filter.
derived_theorem.scope: FOR_ALL B-trajectories and source families R at any composition node whose source-family completeness is supplied by the admitted O2/O3/O4 semantic identities and whose caller premises are separately bound.
derived_theorem.soundness: If Delta in R has width(Delta)>k, then Delta cannot witness any Gamma in up_k(R,B), because Delta preccurlyeq Gamma implies width(Delta)<=width(Gamma), while every Gamma in up_k(R,B) has width<=k.

interpretation_ceiling.failed_refinement_meaning: A failed source refinement of final post-shrink compact width>k is unnecessary as an up_k witness at cap k.
interpretation_ceiling.forbidden_overclaim: Failure of one refinement does not imply that all other interleavings/refinements for the same child pair fail.
interpretation_ceiling.reflection_meaning: Every final full-set state has at least one source refinement of width<=k, conditional on the source family being semantically complete.

published_source.full_set_definition: FS_k(V,B) contains compact B-trajectories Gamma of width<=k dominated by a realizable Delta.
primary_results: Definition of FS_k and up_k in Section 4
published_source.up_k_definition: up_k(R,B) contains compact B-trajectories Gamma of width<=k for which some Delta in R satisfies Delta preccurlyeq Gamma.
published_source.width_lemma: Lemma 3.4: Delta preccurlyeq Gamma implies width(Delta)<=width(Gamma).
